experiments.name: base operand path

latencies.notes: 4 cycles from the base operand rj to the destination, the same latency as a plain load of the same width. The chain has to turn the loaded value back into an address with an add.d, and it also carries one further cycle that the address generator charges for an ALU-produced address, so 2 cycles are subtracted. That extra cycle belongs to the chain, not to the load.

experiments.name: bound operand path

latencies.notes: 4 cycles from the index or bound operand rk to the destination. When the loaded value can feed the address or the range check directly the chain is just the load; when an andi or xori is in the path it reads one cycle more than the helper itself, which is the address-generator premium rather than load latency.

throughput.name: 8 independent addresses
throughput.command: ./bench --unroll 1000 --iters 1000 --warmup 10 --reps 5 --core 0 --init 'addi.d $r20, $sp, -1024; addi.d $r21, $r20, 0; addi.d $r23, $r20, 8; addi.d $r24, $r20, 16; addi.d $r25, $r20, 24; addi.d $r26, $r20, 32; addi.d $r27, $r20, 40; addi.d $r28, $r20, 48; addi.d $r29, $r20, 56; addi.d $r30, $r20, 1024; addi.d $r4, $r0, 1; addi.d $r5, $r0, 2; addi.d $r6, $r0, 3; addi.d $r7, $r0, 4; addi.d $r8, $r0, 5; addi.d $r9, $r0, 6; addi.d $r10, $r0, 7; addi.d $r11, $r0, 8' --asm 'ldle.h $r12, $r21, $r30; ldle.h $r13, $r23, $r30; ldle.h $r14, $r24, $r30; ldle.h $r15, $r25, $r30; ldle.h $r16, $r26, $r30; ldle.h $r17, $r27, $r30; ldle.h $r18, $r28, $r30; ldle.h $r19, $r29, $r30'
throughput.notes: 8 independent lanes: 7.98 core cycles per 8 instructions, CPI 1. Slope method (--unroll 1000, --unroll2 2000).

notes: Latency measured per source operand on LA464: 4 cycles from the base operand rj and 4 cycles from the index or bound operand rk, the same as a plain load. Chains that pass the loaded value through an ALU operation before the next address read one cycle more than that operation, which belongs to the chain. The 64-byte-aligned buffer holds 8 and 0 so the chase stays inside one cache line.
